spacr.assay_panels.axis_layout:
How to label the x axis of one graph.

:param order: conditions in x-axis order.
:param parts: {condition: [(variable, factor), ...]} (see :func:`condition_parts`).
:param style: ``'auto'`` (labels when at most one variable varies along
    this axis, else the matrix), ``'matrix'`` or ``'labels'``.
:param factor_order: matrix rows in display order (raw or display names);
    other rows follow by variable, then first appearance.
:param labels: raw value -> display label, as in :func:`display_label`;
    ``None`` uses no labels.
:returns: ``{'matrix': bool, 'annotations': {row: {condition: '+'/'-'}},
    'labels': {condition: text}, 'constant': [display texts shared by every
    condition], 'varying': [variables]}``.
spacr.assay_panels.condition_parts:
Split a condition into (variable, factor) parts.

:param values: {variable (slot or column): value} of the condition.
:param factors: ``condition_factors`` - {value: [factor, ...]}; a value
    listed there contributes one part per factor (variable ``<var>#<i>``
    for the i-th factor, so backgrounds and genotypes form separate
    variables), any other value is one part of its own variable.
spacr.assay_panels.mark_outliers:
True for points beyond the robust fence of their group.

``mad``: ``|x - median| > fence * 1.4826 * MAD``; ``iqr``: outside
``[Q1 - fence * IQR, Q3 + fence * IQR]``. Groups with fewer than 4 points
or no spread (MAD or IQR 0) keep every point.

:param data: table with one row per point.
:param value: name of the numeric column tested; non-numeric and
    infinite values are ignored.
:param group: column or list of columns defining the groups.
:param method: outlier method in any form accepted by
    :func:`parse_outlier_method`; ``None`` marks nothing.
:returns: boolean Series aligned to ``data.index``.
:raises ValueError: if ``method`` names an unknown outlier method.
spacr.assay_panels.outlier_policy:
Context manager: default outlier method of :func:`bar_spec` inside the block.

``with outlier_policy('mad'): ...`` makes every bar panel built inside
mark and leave out points beyond the robust fence of their group.

:param method: outlier method made the default inside the block, in any
    form accepted by :func:`parse_outlier_method` (``None`` turns marking
    off); the previous default is restored on exit.
spacr.assay_panels.outlier_table:
Points and removed outliers per group (and per ``by`` level).

:param data: table with the ``group`` column and a boolean ``outlier``
    column (see :func:`mark_outliers`).
:param group: column of ``data`` with the condition.
:param order: conditions of the panel; not used to filter or sort the rows.
:param method: outlier method used, in any form accepted by
    :func:`parse_outlier_method`; recorded in the ``method`` and ``fence``
    columns.
:returns: one row per group with ``n_points``, ``n_removed``, ``method``
    and ``fence``.
spacr.assay_panels.pack_brackets:
Stack level of every bracket: shortest spans lowest, brackets on one level never overlap.

:param pairs: chosen pairs with ``group_1`` and ``group_2`` columns, as
    returned by :func:`select_bracket_pairs`.
:param order: conditions in x-axis order; every pair's groups must be in it.
:returns: stack level (0 = lowest) of each row of ``pairs``, in row order.
spacr.assay_panels.parse_outlier_method:
``'mad'`` / ``'iqr'`` (default fences 3.5 and 1.5) or ``'mad:3'`` -> (name, fence); None -> None.

:param method: ``'mad'``, ``'iqr'``, ``'<name>:<fence>'``, ``True``
    (same as ``'mad'``), or ``None`` / ``False`` / ``'none'`` / ``''`` for
    no outlier marking.
:returns: ``(name, fence)`` with ``fence`` a float, or ``None``.
:raises ValueError: if the method name is not ``'mad'`` or ``'iqr'``.
spacr.assay_panels.select_bracket_pairs:
Post hoc pairs that get a bracket, and how many qualifying pairs were left out.

``'one_factor'``: significant pairs that differ in exactly one factor of
``parts`` (same host with another strain, same strain in another host);
every significant pair when the conditions have no factor structure (at
most one variable). ``'all'``: every significant pair. A list of pairs:
those pairs, significant or not. Beyond ``max_n`` the pairs with the
smallest p values are kept.

:param posthoc: post hoc table with ``group_1``, ``group_2``, ``p_adj``
    and ``significance`` columns; ``None`` or empty gives no pairs.
:param order: conditions shown on the axis; pairs with a group outside it
    are dropped.
:returns: (DataFrame of chosen pairs, number of qualifying pairs not drawn).
spacr.assay_panels.shade:
``color`` darkened to ``factor`` (0 black, 1 unchanged), as an RGB tuple.

:param color: any matplotlib colour specification (name, hex string or
    RGB(A) tuple).
:param factor: brightness multiplier applied to each RGB channel; results
    are clipped to [0, 1].
:returns: ``(r, g, b)`` tuple of floats in [0, 1].
spacr.assay_panels.string_parts:
Fallback decomposition: the tokens of the condition string, by position.

:param condition: condition name; converted to text and split on ``sep``.
:returns: ``[('token0', first token), ('token1', second token), ...]``.
spacr.assay_panels.style_axes:
Light horizontal grid behind the data, top and right spines removed.

:param ax: matplotlib ``Axes`` styled in place.
spacr.assay_report:
Standard assay report: A4 pages with pagination, 16-bit tiles and a figure legend.

Used by :func:`spacr.submodules.analyze_recruitment` (``report`` setting) and
written to be reused by other plate assays. Three building blocks:

**Layout engine** (:class:`ReportItem`, :class:`ReportBlock`,
:func:`paginate`, :func:`render_report`). A report is a list of blocks, each a
heading plus panel items. An item is half or full page width with a height in
mm. Items are packed into rows (two half items, or one full item), rows into
A4 portrait pages (210 x 297 mm). A block that does not fit the rest of a page
starts on a new page; a block taller than a page flows on, row by row, with
its heading repeated. Text sizes are fixed in points (never below 5 pt), so a
long report gets more pages, never smaller text. Panels whose condition axis
does not fit the page width are split into chunks of conditions
(:func:`condition_chunks`) drawn as consecutive rows.

**Tiles** (:func:`select_tiles`, :func:`extract_tile`, :func:`render_tile`,
:func:`build_tiles`). Crops of host cells around their mask centroid from the
spaCR merged arrays (image channels then mask planes). The raw crop is written
as a multichannel TIFF with the input dtype and unchanged values; the RGB
composite and the montage are written as 16-bit PNG (OpenCV, BGR order) and
16-bit TIFF (RGB). Only the figure PDF / PNG are 8-bit.

**Legend** (:func:`describe_test`, :func:`filter_sentences`,
:func:`write_legend`). Generic text for every panel: what is plotted, unit of
statistics, n per group, test and why, filters with their counts.

Statistics come from :func:`spacr.assay_panels.select_and_run_test`.
spacr.assay_report.Layout:
Page geometry and type sizes of a report layout (all lengths in mm, fonts in pt).

``compact`` draws 5-6 pt text, slim bars and small markers and first tries
to fit the whole figure on one page (:func:`paginate`); ``spacious`` is
the roomy layout with 8-10 pt text that paginates freely.
spacr.assay_report.Layout.content: Content width in mm: page width minus both side margins.
spacr.assay_report.Layout.usable: Usable height in mm: page height minus top and bottom margins.
spacr.assay_report.Layout.width_mm:
Width in mm of a panel spanning ``frac`` of the content width.

The inter-panel gap is shared, so panels whose fractions add up to 1
fill one row exactly with ``gap`` between them.

:param frac: fraction of the content width (e.g. ``0.5`` for half).
:returns: panel width in mm.
spacr.assay_report.ReportBlock:
A heading plus panel items. Consecutive blocks with the same ``group``
are kept on one page when the compact layout has to paginate.

:param title: heading text drawn above the block's items.
spacr.assay_report.ReportItem:
One panel (or one chunk of a panel) on a page.

:param pid: panel ID (e.g. ``'R1'``); IDs starting with ``'R'`` count as
    main-figure panels.
:param label: text printed in bold in the panel ID strip; empty for none.
:param draw: ``draw(fig, rect)`` with ``rect = (x0, y0, w, h)`` in figure
    fractions; it adds its own axes inside the rect.
:param width: fraction of the content width (or ``'half'``, ``'full'``,
    ``'third'``, ``'quarter'``).
:param height_mm: height reserved on the page, panel ID strip included.
:param min_height_mm: smallest height the one-page fit may shrink it to.
:param new_row: start a new row with this item.
:param show_id: reserve the panel ID strip and print ``label`` in it.
spacr.assay_report.ReportItem.frac: ``width`` as a fraction of the content width (names such as ``'half'`` resolved).
spacr.assay_report.build_assay_report:
Build the standard report: one figure per data version, plate heatmaps, legends.

Two figures, FILTERED then UNFILTERED, each on its own A4 pages: tiles of
that version (``tiles``), the representative object per condition and,
under every value graph, its crop grid (``crops``), the value per
condition at well and replicate level (half page width), the well-level
controls (no statistics), and the figure legend printed under the panels
(following pages when needed). Plate heatmaps follow as an appendix.
Graphs carry no titles or test names: significant post hoc pairs are
brackets with stars; tests are in stats.csv and the legend.

Images (tiles, representative crops, crop grids) come in three versions -
merged colour, channel of interest in grey, and the same with the outline
of every object type - scaled per channel to the 2nd-98th percentile of all
crops of that figure, written as 16-bit PNG/TIFF (``build_tiles``).

:param frames: ``{'unfiltered': df, 'filtered': df}``, one row per ``row_object``.
:param out_dir: output folder for the PDFs, PNGs, ``figure_legend.txt``
    and the ``panels/`` folders.
:param value: column of the frames with the main value per object.
:param group: column of the frames with the condition.
:param order: conditions shown, in display order; rows of other
    conditions are left out.
:param channels: channel numbers that get a mean-intensity panel.
:param labels: raw condition value -> display label (see
    :func:`spacr.assay_panels.display_label`).
:param replicate_column: column with the biological replicate; None
    skips the replicate-level graphs.
:param value_label: axis and legend text of ``value``; default ``value``
    with spaces for underscores.
:param ratio: ``value`` is a ratio: draw a reference line at 1 (and start
    the axis at 1 when every value is at least 1).
:param filter_summary: table of the filter steps (see
    :func:`filter_sentences`), or None.
:param palette: bar colours passed to the bar panels.
:param tiles: None to skip images, else ``merged_dir``, ``mask_dims``,
    ``colour_map``, ``n``, ``size``, ``seed`` and ``mono_channel``.
:param max_conditions_per_row: most conditions in one panel chunk before
    a graph is split over rows.
:param row_object: object type with one row per object in the frames
    (counted by rows in :func:`well_counts`).
:param title: report title, printed in the page headers and the legend.
:param intro: sentences added at the start of each figure legend.
:param name: file stem of the PDFs (``<name>.pdf``,
    ``<name>_figure_<version>.pdf``).
:param count_objects: object types that get an objects-per-well panel;
    None uses the measurements.db object tables, else every object type
    with intensity columns (cytoplasm is always left out).
:param db_path: path to ``measurements.db`` for per-well object counts
    of the unfiltered data; None or a missing file skips them.
:param layout: ``'compact'``, ``'spacious'`` or a :class:`Layout`.
:param well_qc: table from :func:`well_qc_table`; wells failing it get a
    red x on the plate heatmaps.
:param heatmaps: add the plate heatmap appendix.
:param crops: None, or ``{'n': k}`` for representative crops.
:param parts: {condition: [(variable, factor), ...]} for the x axis
    (:func:`spacr.assay_panels.condition_parts`); None splits the
    condition names on '_'.
:param x_axis_style: ``'auto'`` (+/- matrix when two or more variables
    vary on a graph, else labels of the varying part), ``'matrix'``,
    ``'labels'``.
:param factor_order: +/- matrix rows in display order (see
    :func:`spacr.assay_panels.axis_layout`).
:param bracket_pairs: ``'one_factor'``, ``'all'`` or a list of pairs
    (:func:`spacr.assay_panels.select_bracket_pairs`).
:param dpi: resolution of the PNG pages and panel images.
:returns: dict with ``pdf`` (combined), ``figures`` {version: pdf},
    ``png``, ``legend``, ``panels``, ``n_pages``, ``n_figure_pages``,
    ``n_main_pages`` and ``n_legend_pages`` (0: legends are on the figures).
spacr.assay_report.build_tiles:
Pick, crop, render and write the representative tiles of every group.

:param df: object table, one row per host cell, with the ``group``,
    ``object_column`` and ``file_column`` columns.
:param group: column of ``df`` with the condition.
:param order: conditions in display order (montage columns).
:param merged_dir: folder of the merged ``<file_name>.npy`` stacks
    ``(height, width, planes)``.
:param mask_dims: {'cell': plane, 'pathogen': plane, ...}; ``object_column``
    holds the host cell label. Crops are centred on the ``center_object``
    objects of the host cell (pathogen; see :func:`extract_tile`), or on the
    host cell when that mask is absent. At most ``max_attempts`` candidates
    are tried per group.
:param colour_map: {channel index: colour name or (r, g, b) in 0-1} of the
    colour composite (see :func:`render_tile`).
:param out_folder: output folder; ``merged/``, ``mono/``, ``outlines/``
    and ``raw/`` are created inside it.
:param n: tiles per group (montage rows).
:param size: tile edge length in pixels.
:param seed: random seed for the candidate order and the choice of range
    fields.
:param percentiles: (low, high) percentiles of the display range.
:param max_range_fields: largest number of fields sampled for the display
    range when ``range_source='fields'``.
:param object_column: column of ``df`` with the host cell label.
:param file_column: column of ``df`` with the merged stack name (without
    ``.npy``).
:param edge_column: column with the distance of the pathogen object to the
    field edge, used by :func:`select_tiles`.
:param outline_objects: object types to outline; currently every object
    type of ``mask_dims`` is outlined.
:param value_column: column whose group median ``selection='median'``
    uses; also copied into the tile table.
:param center_object: mask role the crops are centred on, or None for the
    host cell.
:param max_attempts: most candidates tried per group.
:param selection: ``'random'`` (seeded, objects away from the edge first)
    or ``'median'`` (objects closest to the median of ``value_column`` in
    their group first: typical objects).
:param range_source: ``'fields'`` (display range from the pixels of the
    fields the tiles come from) or ``'crops'`` (from the pixels of the
    crops themselves, so every crop of the figure is comparable).
:param subdir: folder for the per-crop files; ``montage_name`` the stem of
    the 16-bit montage.
:param montage_name: stem of the 16-bit montage files.
:param mono_channel: channel shown in the two monochrome versions (the
    channel of interest; default the first channel of ``colour_map``).
:param outline_alpha: opacity of the outlines (0-1).
:param gap: width in pixels of the white lines between montage tiles.

Three versions of every crop are written, each a 16-bit set of its own:
``merged/`` (colour composite, no outlines), ``mono/`` (``mono_channel``
in grey, no outlines) and ``outlines/`` (the same grey with the outline of
every object type of the host cell - the cell itself and every other mask
object overlapping it - in its own colour at ``outline_alpha`` opacity).
Each holds ``<subdir>/<group>_<k>.png/.tif`` and ``<montage_name>.png/.tif``
(rows = crops, columns = groups, ``gap`` px white hairlines). ``raw/``
holds the unchanged multichannel crop (all image and mask planes, input
dtype). Display ranges: per channel the ``percentiles`` of the pixels of
every crop of the figure (``range_source='crops'``).
:returns: dict with ``tiles`` {version: {group: [rgb16]}}, ``table`` (one row per
    tile), ``ranges``, ``montage`` (uint16 RGB, rows = tiles, columns =
    groups), ``files`` and ``notes``.
spacr.assay_report.compact_style:
Restyle a drawn panel for the compact layout: 5-6 pt text, slim bars, small dots.

x tick labels are wrapped at word boundaries and drawn at 45 degrees.

:param ax: matplotlib ``Axes`` of a drawn panel, restyled in place.
spacr.assay_report.condition_chunks:
Split the condition order into chunks that fit one page width.

:param order: conditions in display order.
:param per_category_mm: width in mm taken by each condition.
:param fixed_mm: width in mm the panel needs regardless of the number of
    conditions (axis, tick labels, margins).
:param max_per_row: largest number of conditions in one chunk.
:returns: (width, chunks). Without ``layout`` width is ``'half'`` or
    ``'full'`` (spacious); with a layout it is the smallest width fraction
    of ``layout.widths`` (at least ``min_frac``) that holds the panel.
spacr.assay_report.count_source:
How objects of type ``obj`` are counted per well (see :func:`well_counts`).

:param df: analysed frame, one row per ``row_object``.
:param obj: object type to count.
:returns: ``'rows'``, ``'<obj>_prcfo_count'``, ``'<obj>_area'``, or None
    when ``obj`` cannot be counted.
spacr.assay_report.crop_drawer:
Draw callback, height and minimum height (mm) of a crop figure.

The three image versions (merged, channel of interest, channel of interest
with outlines) are drawn side by side when the tiles stay at least
``min_tile_mm`` wide, else stacked. Each version is one tight montage (1 px
hairlines), one column per condition, with the condition labels - or the
+/- matrix of ``axis`` - under the columns. Images are drawn at native
resolution (interpolation 'none').

:param result: :func:`build_tiles` result (``tiles`` per version and
    ``gap``).
:param chunk: conditions drawn, in column order.
:param n: crops per condition (montage rows).
:param size: crop edge length in pixels.
:returns: ``(draw, height_mm, min_height_mm)`` with ``draw(fig, rect)``
    as for :class:`ReportItem`.
spacr.assay_report.crop_items:
Report items of a crop figure, split into condition chunks when wide.

:param pid: panel ID; chunks after the first are labelled
    ``'<pid> (continued)'``.
:param result: :func:`build_tiles` result.
:param order: conditions in display order.
:param n: crops per condition.
:param size: crop edge length in pixels.
:param layout: ``'compact'``, ``'spacious'`` or a :class:`Layout`.
:returns: list of :class:`ReportItem`.
spacr.assay_report.db_object_tables:
Object tables of a measurements.db: tables with plateID, rowID and columnID.

Bookkeeping tables (png_list, intensity_rescale, ...), versioned copies
(``cell_1`` when ``cell`` exists) and ``skip`` (cytoplasm, one per cell)
are left out. cell, nucleus and pathogen come first.

:param db_path: path to the ``measurements.db`` SQLite file (opened read-only).
:returns: list of table names.
spacr.assay_report.db_well_counts:
Rows per well in every object table of measurements.db, for the wells of ``frame``.

:param db_path: path to the ``measurements.db`` SQLite file (opened read-only).
:param frame: analysed table whose wells (``plateID``, ``rowID``,
    ``columnID``) are counted; wells missing from a table count 0.
:param group: column of ``frame`` with the condition of each well.
:returns: long table with ``group``, well keys, ``object_type``,
    ``objects_per_well`` and ``count_source`` (``measurements.db table <t>``).
spacr.assay_report.describe_test:
One sentence: the omnibus test, its result and why it was chosen.

:param test_row: one row of a ``test`` table as a mapping, with ``test``,
    ``p_value``, ``significance`` and optional ``note``.
:returns: the sentence.
spacr.assay_report.display_ranges:
Per channel (low, high) percentiles over pixels of several fields.

:param arrays: image stacks of shape ``(height, width, planes)``, one per
    field; every ``stride``-th pixel is sampled.
:param channels: channel (plane) indices to compute ranges for.
:returns: ``{channel: (low, high)}`` with ``high > low``.
spacr.assay_report.draw_grouped_panel:
Draw a :func:`grouped_spec`: mean ± SD of unit values per object type, dots per unit.

:param ax: matplotlib ``Axes`` to draw into.
:param spec: panel spec returned by :func:`grouped_spec`.
:returns: ``ax``.
spacr.assay_report.draw_heatmap:
Plate heatmap with a colour bar inside ``rect``; failed QC wells marked with a red x.

:param fig: matplotlib ``Figure`` to draw into.
:param rect: ``(x0, y0, w, h)`` in figure fractions.
:param spec: heatmap spec from :func:`heatmap_spec`.
:param plate: plate key of ``spec['matrices']`` drawn.
:returns: the heatmap ``Axes``.
spacr.assay_report.extract_tile:
Crop a ``size`` x ``size`` window around host cell ``label``.

With ``center_plane`` (the pathogen mask plane) the window is centred on
the centroid of the union of the pathogen objects that overlap the host
cell, and the cell is rejected (None) when it has no pathogen object,
when a pathogen object touches the field edge, or when the pathogen
objects do not lie fully inside the crop. Without it the window is
centred on the host cell mask centroid.

:param arr: merged image stack of shape ``(height, width, planes)``
    holding the channels and the object masks.
:param mask_plane: plane index of the host cell mask in ``arr``.
:param label: mask label of the host cell.
:param size: tile edge length in pixels.
:param center_plane: plane index of the pathogen mask, or None to centre
    on the host cell.
:param require_inside: reject crops that reach beyond the field (default:
    True when centring on the pathogen, else False - the crop is then
    zero padded).
:returns: (raw, box, padded) - ``raw`` is the exact in-field slice
    ``arr[y0:y1, x0:x1, :]`` (input dtype, values unchanged), ``box`` is
    ``(y0, y1, x0, x1)`` and ``padded`` the slice zero padded to the full
    tile size (equal to ``raw`` when the crop is inside the field), or
    None.
spacr.assay_report.filter_sentences:
Text of the filter steps in ``filter_summary`` (objects removed / remaining).

:param summary: filter summary table, one row per step with ``step``,
    ``<...>_removed``, ``<...>_remaining`` and optional ``note`` columns; the
    first row is the starting count. None or empty means no filters.
:returns: the sentences joined by spaces.
spacr.assay_report.fit_axes:
Shrink ``ax`` until its tight bounding box (labels, title, legend) fits ``rect``.

:param fig: matplotlib ``Figure`` holding ``ax``.
:param ax: matplotlib ``Axes`` repositioned in place.
:param rect: ``(x0, y0, w, h)`` target box in figure fractions.
spacr.assay_report.get_layout:
Resolve a report layout given by name or as a :class:`Layout`.

:param layout: a :class:`Layout` (returned unchanged) or a layout name,
    ``'compact'`` or ``'spacious'``.
:returns: the matching :class:`Layout`.
:raises ValueError: if ``layout`` is not a :class:`Layout` or a known name.
spacr.assay_report.grouped_spec:
Grouped bars (one colour per object type) with one test per object type.

Outlier points are marked per object type and group with the active
:class:`spacr.assay_panels.outlier_policy` (``outlier`` column) and left
out of the drawing and the tests.

:param data: long table with ``group``, ``object_type`` and ``value``
    columns, one row per unit (e.g. from :func:`well_intensity_long`).
:param group: column of ``data`` with the condition.
:param order: conditions in display order.
:param objects: object types drawn, one bar colour each.
:returns: panel spec dict (``kind='grouped'``) with the data, styling and
    per-object-type ``stats``.
spacr.assay_report.heatmap_spec:
Plate heatmap of well values; ``failed`` = {(plate, row, column)} drawn with a red x.

:param data: well-level table with the well key columns and ``value``;
    duplicate wells are averaged.
:param value: column with the well value.
:param title: heatmap title.
:returns: heatmap spec dict (``kind='heatmap'``) with ``matrices``,
    ``vrange`` and ``failed``.
spacr.assay_report.montage16:
Rows = tile rank, columns = groups; white 16-bit gaps; missing tiles stay black.

:param tiles: {group: [uint16 RGB tile of shape (size, size, 3)]}.
:param order: groups in column order.
:param n: number of rows (tiles per group).
:param size: tile edge length in pixels.
:returns: uint16 RGB montage array.
spacr.assay_report.object_colours:
Colour per object type: fixed for cell/nucleus/cytoplasm/pathogen, others in name order.

:param objects: object type names.
:returns: ``{object type: hex colour}``.
spacr.assay_report.object_qc_mask:
Object-level QC: per plate, condition group and object type, objects beyond the robust fence.

Area and channel mean intensities are compared on log scale (values <= 0
are never flagged) with the objects of the same plate and ``group``
value, or of the whole plate when ``group`` is None or holds fewer than
``min_objects`` objects there.

:param df: object-level measurement table, one row per object.
:returns: (keep mask, summary with ``object_type``, ``measure``,
    ``column``, ``objects_removed``, ``objects``, ``qc_group`` and
    ``groups_on_plate_fallback`` - an object can fail several measures).
spacr.assay_report.object_types:
Object prefixes with ``<obj>_channel_<c>_mean_intensity`` columns.

cell, nucleus, cytoplasm and pathogen come first, any other prefix
(organelles ...) after them in alphabetical order.

:param df: object-level measurement table.
spacr.assay_report.paginate:
Place blocks on A4 pages.

Spacious: blocks flow over pages; a block that does not fit the rest of a
page starts on a new page (unless most of it fits), a block taller than
a page flows on row by row with its heading repeated.

Compact (``fit_one_page``): the whole figure is first fitted on one page
by shrinking panel heights towards their minimum. If that fails, whole
block groups (consecutive blocks sharing ``group``, e.g. the control
blocks before and after filtering) are packed page by page, each page
shrunk to fit; a group that cannot fit one page on its own flows row by
row as in the spacious layout.

:param blocks: :class:`ReportBlock` objects in page order; blocks without
    items are skipped.
:returns: one list per page of placements, each a dict with ``kind``
    (``'heading'`` or ``'item'``), ``text`` / ``item`` and ``rect_mm``
    ``(x0, y_top, w, h)`` measured from the top-left page corner.
spacr.assay_report.plate_heatmap_items:
One report item per plate of a heatmap spec.

:param pid: panel ID of the heatmap; plates after the first are labelled
    ``'<pid> (<plate>)'``.
:param spec: heatmap spec from :func:`heatmap_spec` (``matrices`` holds one
    rows x columns array per plate).
:returns: list of :class:`ReportItem`, one per plate.
spacr.assay_report.plate_matrices:
{plate: (matrix rows x columns, nan where no data)} of well values.

:param data: one row per well with the well key columns and ``value``.
:param value: column with the well value.
:returns: ``{plate: 2-D float array}``.
spacr.assay_report.plate_shape:
Standard plate layout holding the given row / column numbers.

:param rows: 1-based row numbers of the wells.
:param cols: 1-based column numbers of the wells.
:returns: ``(n_rows, n_cols)`` of the smallest 96-, 384- or 1536-well
    plate that holds them, else the largest numbers themselves.
spacr.assay_report.qc_object_types:
Object types with an area or a channel mean-intensity column.

:param df: object-level measurement table.
:returns: object types from :func:`object_types`, then other prefixes that
    have ``<obj>_area`` and ``<obj>_perimeter`` columns.
spacr.assay_report.render_report:
Draw paginated placements, then the legend on pages of its own, into one PDF.

:param pages: page placements as returned by :func:`paginate`.
:param pdf_path: output PDF file; its folder is created if needed and the
    PNG pages are written next to it.
:returns: ``{'pdf', 'png': [paths], 'n_pages', 'n_figure_pages', 'n_legend_pages'}``.
    PNG files are ``<stem>.png`` for page 1 and ``<stem>_page_NN.png``
    for the next pages.
spacr.assay_report.render_tile:
16-bit RGB composite of an image crop.

:param crop: image crop of shape ``(h, w, planes)``; channels are indexed
    by plane.
:param colour_map: {channel index: colour name or (r, g, b) in 0-1}.
:param ranges: {channel index: (low, high)} display range, the same for
    every tile.
:param outlines: [(binary mask, (r, g, b) in 0-1)], drawn 1 px wide.
:param alpha: opacity of the outlines over the image (0-1).
:returns: uint16 array (h, w, 3), RGB order.
spacr.assay_report.resolve_mask_dims:
Plane index of each object mask: ``overrides``, else the plane layout
sidecar of the merged folder, else the last ``len(names)`` planes in order.

:param merged_dir: folder of the merged ``.npy`` stacks whose plane layout
    sidecar is read.
:param names: object roles (e.g. ``'cell'``, ``'pathogen'``) in mask-plane
    order.
:param n_planes: number of planes in each merged stack.
:returns: ``{role: plane index}``.
spacr.assay_report.save_crop_panel:
PDF/PNG of every version (``<version>/<stem>_<version>``) and of all three (``<stem>``).

:param folder: output folder; one subfolder per image version is created.
:param stem: file stem of the saved figures.
:param result: :func:`build_tiles` result.
:param order: conditions in column order.
:param n: crops per condition.
:param size: crop edge length in pixels.
spacr.assay_report.save_heatmap_panel:
Save a heatmap spec as its own panel folder, plates stacked top to bottom.

:param out_dir: parent folder of the panel folder.
:param pid: panel ID, the first part of the folder name.
:param name: panel name, the second part of the folder name.
:param spec: heatmap spec from :func:`heatmap_spec`; its ``data`` is
    written as ``data.csv``.
:returns: folder path (see :func:`write_panel_folder`).
spacr.assay_report.save_spec_panel:
Save a bar / grouped spec as its own panel folder at full size.

:param out_dir: parent folder of the panel folder.
:param pid: panel ID, the first part of the folder name.
:param name: panel name, the second part of the folder name.
:param spec: bar or :func:`grouped_spec` panel spec; its ``data`` and
    :func:`stats_long` tables are written as ``data.csv`` and ``stats.csv``.
:returns: folder path (see :func:`write_panel_folder`).
spacr.assay_report.select_median:
Candidates per group ordered by distance to the group median of ``value`` (typical first).

:param df: object table with the ``group`` and ``value`` columns.
:param group: column of ``df`` with the condition.
:param order: conditions to pick from.
:param value: numeric column whose group median is used; rows without a
    finite value are dropped.
:returns: {group value: DataFrame of candidates in pick order}, each with
    the median in ``attrs['median']``.
spacr.assay_report.select_tiles:
Random objects per group, objects away from the field edge first.

An object is preferred when ``edge_column`` (distance of the centre of
its pathogen object to the field edge) is at least half the tile size,
so the crop can lie inside the field. Candidates are shuffled with
``seed``; the caller takes the first ``n`` that pass
:func:`extract_tile`.

:param df: object table with the ``group`` column.
:param group: column of ``df`` with the condition.
:param order: conditions to pick from, in display order.
:param n: number of tiles wanted per condition; not used for the
    ordering itself (every candidate is returned).
:returns: {group value: DataFrame of candidates in pick order}.
spacr.assay_report.spec_items:
Report items for a bar / grouped spec, split into condition chunks if needed.

:param pid: panel ID; chunks after the first are labelled
    ``'<pid> (continued)'``.
:param spec: bar or :func:`grouped_spec` panel spec.
:param max_per_row: largest number of conditions in one chunk.
:param group_size: number of panels drawn side by side as one group (the
    recruitment panels, the channel panels ...); in the compact layout a
    group of up to four shares one row in equal widths.
spacr.assay_report.stats_long:
Test, assumptions, post hoc and descriptive tables of a spec in one long table.

:param spec: panel spec (bar or :func:`grouped_spec`) with ``stats``.
:returns: tables stacked with a ``table`` column naming the source table
    (and ``object_type`` for grouped specs).
spacr.assay_report.text_items:
One report item per legend paragraph (flows over pages with the panels).

:param paragraphs: legend paragraphs; empty ones are skipped.
:param layout: ``'compact'``, ``'spacious'`` or a :class:`Layout`.
:returns: list of :class:`ReportItem` without ID strips.
spacr.assay_report.well_column_long:
Well means of one column per object type in long format ({object type: column}).

:param df: object-level measurement table with well key columns.
:param group: column of ``df`` with the condition of each row.
:param columns: ``{object type: column of df}``; missing columns are skipped.
:param value_name: name of the output value column.
:returns: columns ``group``, well keys, ``object_type``, ``column``,
    ``value_name``, ``n_objects``.
spacr.assay_report.well_counts:
Objects of type ``obj`` per well in the analysed frame.

The frame has one row per ``row_object`` (the host cell in recruitment):
rows are counted for that type; other types sum ``<obj>_prcfo_count``
(objects of that type merged into each row) when present, else count rows
with a ``<obj>_area`` value. Counting from the frame, not the database
tables, means the count follows every filter applied to the frame.

:param df: analysed frame, one row per ``row_object``, with well key columns.
:param group: column of ``df`` with the condition of each row.
:param obj: object type to count (e.g. ``'cell'``, ``'pathogen'``).
:returns: one row per (``group``, well) with ``objects_per_well`` and
    ``count_source``; empty when ``obj`` cannot be counted.
spacr.assay_report.well_intensity_long:
Mean intensity of ``channel`` per well for every object type (long format).

:param df: object-level measurement table with well key columns.
:param group: column of ``df`` with the condition of each row.
:param channel: channel number ``c`` of the
    ``<obj>_channel_<c>_mean_intensity`` columns.
:returns: columns ``group``, well keys, ``object_type``, ``column``,
    ``mean_intensity``, ``n_objects``.
spacr.assay_report.well_qc_table:
Well-level QC: every well against the other wells of its condition group on its plate.

Per well, for every object type: object count (rows for ``row_object``,
else the sum of ``<obj>_prcfo_count``), median ``<obj>_area`` and median
``<obj>_channel_<c>_mean_intensity`` per channel. A well fails when any
measure lies more than ``mad`` x 1.4826 x MAD from the median of the
reference wells (measures with MAD 0 flag nothing). The reference is the
wells of the same plate and the same ``group`` value (so real differences
between conditions are not flagged), or the whole plate when ``group`` is
None or its group has fewer than ``min_wells`` wells on that plate.

:param df: object-level measurement table with well key columns.
:param channels: channel numbers checked for intensity; None = every
    channel with a mean-intensity column for the object type.
:param measures: subset of ``('count', 'area', 'intensity')``; None = all.
:param mad: fence in robust z units (multiples of 1.4826 x MAD).
:param row_object: object type with one row per object in ``df``.
:param well_keys: columns identifying a well.
:param group: column of ``df`` with the condition group, or None (per plate).
:param min_wells: smallest number of wells of a group on a plate used as
    its own reference.
:returns: one row per well: well keys, ``qc_group``, ``qc_reference``,
    ``<measure>`` and ``<measure>_z`` columns, ``well_qc_pass`` and
    ``well_qc_reason`` (measures that failed).
spacr.assay_report.write_legend:
Write the figure legend as a UTF-8 text file, one blank line between paragraphs.

Empty paragraphs are dropped and the others stripped of surrounding
whitespace; the folder of ``path`` is created if needed.

:param path: output text file.
:param paragraphs: legend paragraphs in order.
:returns: the text written (without the final newline).
spacr.assay_report.write_panel_folder:
One panel folder: ``<Rnn_name>.pdf/.png``, ``data.csv`` and ``stats.csv``.

:param out_dir: parent folder; the panel folder is created inside it.
:param pid: panel ID (e.g. ``'R01'``), the first part of the folder and
    file stem.
:param name: panel name, the second part of the stem (see
    :func:`spacr.assay_panels.panel_folder_name`).
:param draw: ``draw(fig, rect)`` as for :class:`ReportItem`.
:param size_mm: ``(width, height)`` of the saved figure in mm.
:returns: folder path.
spacr.assay_report.write_rgb16:
Write an RGB uint16 array as ``<stem>.png`` (OpenCV, BGR order) and ``<stem>.tif``.

:param stem: output path without extension.
:param rgb: image array of shape ``(h, w, 3)`` in RGB order, cast to uint16.
:returns: the two file paths.
spacr.submodules._field_background.one: Background median per channel of one field, read from its merged array.
spacr.submodules._report_grouping.add_gr: Add the report grouping column to ``frame`` (a copy); unchanged when it is ``condition``.
